items.title: Added flag for whether to fail on invalid environments during project interpreter discovery
items.reason: Direct proposed fix for astral-sh/uv#19832: for `uv lock` only, treat an invalid project environment as unavailable and fall back to interpreter discovery.

items.title: Add `--active` flag for `uv lock`
items.reason: Reproduces the same failure and proposes the reporter’s alternative `--active` workaround. A maintainer rejected that direction and closed it because astral-sh/uv#19832 is the canonical tracker.

items.title: Added `--active` flag for `uv lock` command
items.reason: Implements the alternative bypass from astral-sh/uv#21009 for the same nested `.venv` reproduction, but the linked maintainer decision favors ignoring an invalid environment during locking instead.

related.search_scope: Searched issues and pull requests using the exact error fragments, `uv lock` plus `.venv` and virtual-environment terms, interpreter discovery and fallback vocabulary, active-environment terms, and multiple or nested environment concepts. Inspected linked chains for astral-sh/uv#19832, astral-sh/uv#21009, astral-sh/uv#9423, astral-sh/uv#13235, and their pull requests. astral-sh/uv#9423 and merged astral-sh/uv#9427 were ruled out because they concern `uv sync` and an empty mounted directory; astral-sh/uv#13986 and astral-sh/uv#11219 involve invalid partial environments caused by deletion or concurrency; astral-sh/uv#9906 concerns named-environment workflows but not `uv lock` failing.

type_reason: Repository source confirms that `uv lock` calls project interpreter discovery, which inspects `.venv`; a nonempty directory without a Python executable is returned as an invalid-project-environment error before global or managed Python fallback. Locking does not synchronize that environment, and a maintainer explicitly stated it should not fail in this case. No older canonical report tracks this exact bug; astral-sh/uv#19833 was opened in response to it, so it does not make the issue a duplicate.
summary: This is the canonical bug report for `uv lock` failing on a nonempty invalid `.venv`. astral-sh/uv#19833 directly proposes the intended fallback behavior. The later active-environment issue astral-sh/uv#21009 was closed in favor of this report, while its implementation astral-sh/uv#21010 remains open but follows the direction maintainers declined.
draft_response: Thanks for the clear reproduction. `uv lock` should not fail just because the project environment path exists but is not a valid virtual environment; locking can fall back to a compatible system or managed Python without synchronizing `.venv`. We’ll keep astral-sh/uv#19832 as the canonical tracker. astral-sh/uv#19833 is the open proposed fix for that behavior. We do not plan to add `--active` as the workaround; astral-sh/uv#21009 was closed in favor of fixing the invalid-environment handling directly.
